question: Which of the following is likely to shift the long-run aggregate supply curve to the right?
options: A nation that devotes more resources to nondurable consumption goods rather than durable capital goods
Research that improves the productivity of labor and capital
More restrictive trade policies
Annual limits to immigration of foreign citizens

question: Suppose an economy is in long-run equilibrium at the full-employment level of output. If government spending then increases
options: an inflationary gap is created because the aggregate demand curve shifts to the right
an inflationary gap is created because the aggregate supply curve shifts to the right
an inflationary gap is created because potential GDP shifts to the left
a recessionary gap is created because the aggregate supply curve shifts to the left

question: If Matt's total utility from consuming bratwurst increased at a constant rate, no matter how many bratwurst Matt consumed, what would Matt's demand curve for bratwurst look like?
options: Vertical
Horizontal
Downward sloping
Upward sloping

question: An effective price ceiling in the market for good X likely results in
options: a persistent surplus of good X.
a persistent shortage of good X.
an increase in the demand for good Y, a substitute for good X.
a decrease in the demand for good Z, a complement with good X.

question: A negative or contractionary supply shock will
options: shift the Phillips curve to the left.
shift the investment demand curve to the right.
shift the money demand curve to the right.
shift the Phillips curve to the right.

question: If current real GDP is $5000 and full employment real GDP is at $4000 which of the following combinations of policies is the most likely to have brought the economy to this point?
options: A decrease in taxes and a lower discount rate
An increase in government spending and an increase in taxes
A decrease in taxes and selling bonds in an open market operation
An increase in government spending and an increase in the discount rate

question: Land refers to
options: all productive resources.
all natural resources.
farmland only.
real estate.

question: When a firm is earning a normal profit from the production of a good, it is true that
options: total revenues from production are equal to explicit costs.
explicit costs are equal to implicit costs.
total revenues from production are equal to implicit costs.
total revenues from production are equal to the sum of explicit and implicit costs.

question: Which of the following is a component of the M 1 measure of money supply?
options: Savings deposits
Gold bullion
Cash and coins
30-year Treasury certificates

question: Which is the best way to describe the AS curve in the long run?
options: Always vertical in the long run.
Always upward sloping because it follows the Law of Supply.
Always horizontal.
Always downward sloping.

question: Which of the following most likely increases aggregate demand in the United States?
options: An American entrepreneur founds and locates a software company in London.
The U.S. military closes a military base in California.
The Chinese government makes it increasingly difficult for American firms to export goods to China.
A Mexican entrepreneur founds and locates a software company in St. Louis.

question: Which of the following is a tool used by the Fed to increase the money supply?
options: A lower discount rate.
Selling Treasury securities to commercial banks.
A higher reserve ratio.
A lower personal income tax rate.

question: If the economy is experiencing a recession how will a plan to decrease taxes for consumers and increase spending on government purchases affect real gross domestic product (GDP) and the price level?
options: real GDP rises and the price level falls.
real GDP falls and the price level rises.
real GDP rises and the price level rises.
real GDP falls and the price level falls.

question: Classical economists generally believe that I. wages fluctuate quickly II. Say's law does not hold III. input and output prices will stay in line with each other IV. the government should not worry about maintaining aggregate demand at an adequate level
options: II and IV only
I III and IV only
I and IV only
II and III only

question: If the economy is in disequilibrium where the price level is such that the aggregate quantity of products demanded exceeds the aggregate quantity of products supplied then
options: prices will be driven upward to restore equilibrium.
supply will increase.
demand will decrease.
supply will decrease.

question: Which of the following represents a measure of a firm's monopoly pricing or market power, i.e., the larger the value of the index, the greater the firm's market pricing power?
options: (MC-P)/MC
(MC-P)/P
(P-MC)/P
(P-MC)/MC

question: If firms are entering an industry that is monopolistically competitive, we would expect
options: the demand for existing firms to shift rightward.
the market price of the product to increase.
the demand for existing firms to become more inelastic.
the demand for existing firms to shift leftward.

question: Which of the following will have an effect on GDP?
options: You lose $50 betting with a friend.
You fix your brother's car without buying any new parts.
Your father's firm makes computers and exports them to China.
You buy 1000 shares of stock in a corporation.

question: You buy 100 shares in XYZ Corporation on the Internet and your broker charges you $29.95.
options: This will increase the investment component of GDP and therefore overall GDP.
This has no effect on GDP.
This will increase GDP by $29.95.
This will increase GDP by the cost of the shares minus $29.95.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major cost of inflation?
options: Resources will be misallocated.
Wealth will be redistributed.
Savings will be discouraged.
Real incomes will fall.
